target_customer: Large enterprises buying HR, IT and finance employee service automation
problem: Employees file repetitive HR and IT questions and tickets that support teams answer by hand.
business_model: B2B enterprise SaaS subscription per deployment
product_category: Enterprise conversational AI and AI colleagues for back office

founders.name: Adit Jain
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and CEO in TechCrunch Sept 2018.

technical_complexity.rationale: Natural language understanding over messy HR content plus integrations with Oracle, SAP and NetSuite and chat channels; standard engineering with some hard NLP parts in 2018.

defensibility.rationale: Deep integrations with HR systems and enterprise deployments create some lock in; the NLP itself was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: HCM and service desk suites added assistants; Moveworks, a rival, was acquired by ServiceNow, and Leena reportedly approached ServiceNow about part of it in 2025 (Axios).

market_need_then: TechCrunch reported 16 enterprise customers in September 2018 with a goal of 50 within 12 to 18 months.

branding.name_origin: Derivative of Lena Forsen, the Swedish model whose image is a standard computer vision test picture; founders had placed runners up in a computer vision competition (company blog).

identity.mascot_or_character: Personified AI colleagues Harrison (HR), Iris (IT) and Fiona (Finance) on the current site

branding.community_and_virality: Gartner Leader claim and large named customers on site; no consumer virality evidence.

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable origin story and personified product names, but enterprise software brand with limited press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Leena AI pivoted from a chatbot builder into an enterprise HR assistant, took a 2 million dollar seed after YC Summer 2018, then raised 8 million in 2020 and 30 million in 2021 as enterprise deals grew. It later broadened to IT and finance AI colleagues and took a strategic investment from IBM Ventures in 2026, so it is a steady enterprise growth company facing larger suites and rivals such as Moveworks.
notes: Series A and B details come from search snippets of the company blog and Futurum; those pages were not opened. ZoomInfo names B Capital as Series B lead, other outlets Bessemer; Bessemer used. CB Insights total of $40.12M over 5 rounds, so a small round (about $2M around 2021 before the VadR acquihire) may be missing. Caplight estimates $250M valuation tied to Series B, unverified, not recorded. IBM Ventures investment dated 2026-10 from a single secondary outlet; amount undisclosed. No competitor source dated near 2018 found; Moveworks Series A was April 2019, after the batch, so not listed. Founders' education and prior employers not found. YC page lists 500 team size; founded year 2015 per TechCrunch Chatteron start.
